text: People in general take characters, as they do most things, upon trust, rather than be at the trouble of examining them themselves; and the decisions of four or five fashionable people, in every place, are final, more particularly with regard to characters, which all can hear, and but few judge of.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter CXXVII, to his son, London, January 14, Old Style 1751
